chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from al-Nadr ibn Qirwash, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Umrah with Hajj (Hajj al-Tamattu'), for which the sacrifice (Nusk) became obligatory upon him. He sought it but did not find it, while he was wealthy, in good condition, but weak for fasting. What should he do? He said: 'He should pay the price of the sacrifice to someone who will slaughter it on his behalf in Mecca, if he intends to proceed to his family, and let him slaughter on his behalf in Dhu al-Hijjah.' I said: 'Indeed, he paid it to someone who slaughtered it on his behalf, but did not find a sacrifice in Dhu al-Hijjah, and found one after that.' He said: 'He should not slaughter on his behalf except in Dhu al-Hijjah, even if he delays it to next year.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for Hajj al-Tamattu' if the sacrifice is not found or the pilgrim is too weak to fast?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific procedure for the *Nusk* (sacrifice) of Hajj al-Tamattu' when the pilgrim is wealthy but physically unable to fast the expiation. The Imam emphasizes that the sacrifice must be performed in Dhu al-Hijjah, and if missed, it is deferred to the following year rather than being compensated immediately, highlighting the strict temporal adherence to the sacred months in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the distinction between the sacrifice of Hajj and other expiations, requiring the actual slaughter during the designated time even if delegated to another.
